rocm_cache.tar.gz -- prebuilt object files with no source in this repository
============================================================================

What it is
----------
Two ELF relocatable objects, one per libstdc++ ABI:

  rocm_cache.o        389048 bytes  built 2022-08-05 by "lzhengning"
                      GCC (GNU) 7.3.1 20180303 (Red Hat 7.3.1-5)
                      old ABI (no _GLIBCXX_USE_CXX11_ABI symbols)

  rocm_cache_cxx11.o  449840 bytes  built 2022-08-05 by "lzhengning"
                      GCC (Ubuntu 9.4.0-1ubuntu1~20.04.1) 9.4.0
                      new ABI (514 __cxx11 symbols)

archive SHA-256: 77c52dc063b71d23b508f70f9cd30649d7aa8ff040dc480848883579608a6999

`rocm_compiler.py:install_rocm_jittor_core` picks one of the two by reading
`gcc -v` for `--with-default-libstdcxx-abi`, extracts it next to this file, and
links it into a module that is then loaded into the running process. Between
them the objects define, among ~620 symbols:

  jittor::process_rocm(...)
  jittor::rocm_jittor_op_compiler(...)
  jittor::process_cub / process_cudnn / process_cublas(...)

`rocm_jittor.h` declares `rocm_jittor_op_compiler`; nothing in this repository
defines it. The same is true of the others. **The source for these objects is
not in this repository and no build script for them exists here.**

Why this file exists
--------------------
`MANIFEST.in` has `recursive-include python/jittor/extern *`, so this archive
is in every Jittor wheel -- including wheels installed on machines that have no
AMD GPU and will never load it. A binary that ships to every user, is linked
into their process, and has neither source nor build instructions is not
something anyone can review, rebuild, or patch. Recording what is known about
it is the minimum; it is not a substitute for the source.

What has to happen before this is acceptable
--------------------------------------------
Either of:

  1. The source is contributed to this repository together with a build script,
     and these objects are built like everything else; or
  2. The archive is moved out of the wheel and into the third-party download
     manifest (`jittor_utils/manifest.py`), fetched on demand by the machines
     that actually have ROCm, and verified against the SHA-256 above -- the
     same treatment MKL, cub, cutt and NCCL already get.

Until then `tests/structure/test_rocm_blob_provenance.py` pins the archive's
digest, so the bytes cannot change without someone saying so.
